text:
Priya M.: ok team — we need a tight battlecard refresh for next week's webinar (Wed 10am PT). goal: field + SDRs can rebut cloud AI "managed endpoints" claims in 60s.
Matt G.: love it. can we prioritize 3 competitor plays: cloud platforms, LLM APIs, infra vendors? keep one-pager per play.
Jen L.: yes. I'll own the LLM API play (latency vs cost tradeoffs + model control).
Alex R.: I'll drop the benchmark narrative for infra vendors — show throughput/latency per $ with our batching + kv cache numbers.
Sam H.: field needs two quick soundbites: 1) why dedicated capacity beats bursty managed endpoints, 2) how routing + fallback keeps apps up during outages.
Priya M.: Perfect. For webinar hooks we want: "How we cut token cost 3x without losing quality" + "Keeping SLAs when clouds spike".
Matt G.: Can we add a one-liner vs cloud: "Same API shape, predictable performance, lower tail latency" — short and punchy.
Jen L.: Drafting claims — need proof points. Suggest: 99th percentile latency charts, cost-per-1M tokens with/without batching, and a short customer quote.
Alex R.: Bench numbers coming. Early run: gpt-like open model served on A100 equiv. With continuous batching + prefix cache we see 2.8x token cost improvement and 35% lower p99. I'll paste artifacts when ready.
benchbot: benchmark run complete: https://redwood.internal/bench/4126 — summary: 2.8x cost, 34% p99 improvement, stable throughput 1.7k rps per node.
Sam H.: Nice. For field one-pager, pls include a tiny decision tree: customer size -> choose Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Field wants copy they can read in <45s.
Priya M.: Agreed. Also include rebut lines: e.g., competitor: "We scale infinitely, no capacity planning" -> rebut: "Infinite promises mean noisy neighbor tail latency; our Dedicated option gives guaranteed throughput + SLA."
Matt G.: Add an objection handler for procurement: "Why pay reserved vs spot?" answer: "Unit economics + predictable billing for customer-facing features."
Jen L.: For the LLM API play, include 3 micro-snippets: cost comparison table, code parity example (same API call), and a migration checklist. I'll paste code sample: 
```
// same call shape
POST /v1/generate
{ model: "redwood/rlm-1", prompt: "..." }
```
Priya M.: Nice. Keep language non-technical in the top half, then attach appendix with charts + ascii table. Field likes the TL;DR first.
Alex R.: One more idea: performance routing story — show how policy-based routing can automatically fall back to cheaper variants during peak and preserve SLAs for premium users. A simple diagram will sell it.
Sam H.: For webinar slides: 2 slides for each competitor play (claim, refutation + data). 3 live demo steps: run simple request, show p99, flip to fallback. 10 min demo total.
Matt G.: Call to action: Post-webinar: auto-send battlecard + 3 rebut-snippets to registrants and to CRM with lead-stage tag. Ops: Sam, can you own the CRM flow?
Sam H.: yes, I'll wire it up — need final one-pagers by Mon EOD.
Priya M.: timeline recap: Jen + Alex deliver drafts by Fri, Sam finalizes field handoff Mon, review Tue morning, webinar Wed 10am PT.
Jen L.: I'll add short FAQs: "Do you need to re-train?" "No — model variants + quantization profiles handled at serving."
Matt G.: Add competitor soundbites: "They push model upgrades without regressions" -> our response: "Rollouts, canary, and automatic fallback to verified checkpoints protects quality and uptime."
Priya M.: Great. Next actions: Jen (LLM API one-pager), Alex (bench artifacts + p99 chart png), Sam (CRM + TL;DR flow), Matt (sales one-liners). Everyone drop drafts in #marketing-assets by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
Jen L.: Will do.
Alex R.: uploading bench pngs now.
benchbot: upload complete: /assets/bench/4126/p99_chart.png
Sam H.: copying notes to our playbook, will ping when CRM flow is live.
Priya M.: Thanks all — this is in good shape. We'll reconvene Tue 9:30am PT to finalize slides.
